Partial covariate effects for a fitted statnnet model

Source: R/pce.R
pce.Rd

Computes finite differences of the partial-dependence function. The results describe the fitted response surface and should not be interpreted as causal effects. For correlated predictors, some evaluated combinations may have little support in the data.

Usage

pce(
  object,
  variable,
  values = NULL,
  d = NULL,
  length_out = 101L,
  type = c("curve", "average"),
  uncertainty = c("delta", "simulation", "none"),
  level = 0.95,
  nsim = 1000L,
  seed = NULL,
  by = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A statnnet object.

variable

Name of an original predictor.

values

Values at which to evaluate a continuous predictor. By default, an evenly spaced grid keeps the baseline and finite-difference comparison within the observed range. User-supplied values are used unchanged and may extrapolate.

d

Finite-difference step for a continuous predictor. The default is one observed standard deviation. Binary predictors are always compared from 0 to 1 and factors against their first level.

length_out

Number of grid points for a continuous predictor.

type

"curve" for evaluations over values, or "average" for a point summary averaged over observed predictor values. Average effects may compare values beyond the observed range near a boundary.

uncertainty

One of "delta", "simulation", or "none".

level

Pointwise confidence level. Curve intervals are not simultaneous confidence bands.

nsim

Number of simulation draws when uncertainty = "simulation".

seed

Optional simulation seed.

by

Optional name of a second predictor at whose values the PCE is evaluated. Continuous predictors use their observed mean minus and plus one standard deviation. Binary predictors use both fitted levels.

Value

A data frame of class "statnnet_pce".

Examples

data("auto_mpg", package = "statnnet")
example_data <- auto_mpg
example_data$mpg <- as.numeric(scale(example_data$mpg))
example_data$weight <- as.numeric(scale(example_data$weight))
set.seed(3)
fit <- nnet::nnet(
  mpg ~ weight + origin,
  data = example_data,
  size = 1,
  linout = TRUE,
  decay = 0.1,
  Hess = TRUE,
  maxit = 500,
  trace = FALSE
)
model <- statnnet(fit, data = example_data, response = "continuous")
pce(model, "weight", length_out = 5)

#> 5   weight     <NA>  1.54580798    1 -0.2142032 0.06056191 -0.3329024
